clue.text: Can and must arrange for study

indicators.note: to arrange things is to put them in a new order, so the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: An instruction about what has to be sorted out before someone can settle down to study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrange' shuffles CAN and MUST together; 'and' just joins the two words. A sanctum is a private room, a sense of 'study'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a private retreat or den, the kind of room a scholar shuts themselves away in to work.

clue.text: Pays the bill for furniture

explanation.surface: Someone settling up after buying pieces for the home.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to pay off a debt, and a settle is a high-backed wooden bench, so the plural is a set of furnishings.

clue.text: Troops have spirits raised, here in Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so its letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common abbreviation for army troops
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Soldiers in Africa cheering themselves up with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns REGIN upwards; in a down entry that reads backwards, giving the name of a West African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked country of West Africa, so it is a place found on that continent.

clue.text: Learn toy could come from Innsbruck

indicators.note: the letters could come out as a new word when rearranged, signalling a reshuffle of the fodder

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a toy for learning might have been made in the Austrian Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: Innsbruck is the capital of the Austrian region of Tyrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Innsbruck is the main city of the Tyrol, so anything originating there is described with the region's adjective.

clue.text: Skylight's low point

parts.note: to low is to make the sound of a cow, to moo
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A complaint about the worst thing in a roof window.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', a link. 'low point' looks like one phrase meaning the bottom, but it splits into a cow's call and a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon is the light that shines in the night sky.

clue.text: Hide this — or release it

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction to conceal something or let it go.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete is both to stash away out of sight and, in biology, to discharge a fluid from a gland: two separate senses.

clue.text: Place in which we learn porpoises are gathered, given space

parts.note: a group of porpoises or dolphins is called a school
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A marine-themed picture of a classroom where porpoises assemble with space to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A classroom is the place where pupils are taught their lessons.

clue.text: This plating on medal is capital!

parts.note: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Someone admiring the shiny finish on a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British honour; 'capital!' looks like an old-fashioned cry of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromium is the metal electroplated onto car trim and taps to give a bright finish.

clue.text: A third of Europe having typical hotchpotch of trees

indicators.note: a third of a six-letter word is its opening two letters
a hotchpotch is a jumbled mixture, so the letters of the word typical are jumbled

explanation.surface: A remark that one third of Europe is covered in a typical mixed jumble of woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A third of' takes EU, the first two of six letters; 'hotchpotch' scrambles TYPICAL into CALYPTI. 'having' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum trees of Australia make up this genus, whose Latin plural names a stand of them.

clue.text: Never reaching a conclusion

parts.note: read as about an argument or story that drags on, but really describing something that has no end at all

explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting has no finish, so it never comes to a close.

clue.text: Flying one could get tight more easily

indicators.note: taken loosely or easily, the letters of the two words are arranged freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who is drunk might more readily take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' means drunk on the surface; here it is just letters, rearranged with MORE. 'could get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland biplane of this name was a famous training aircraft, so it is something that flies.

clue.text: Dog turned on the man, it's gathered

indicators.note: turned round, the word for the dog is read backwards

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A dog rounding on a man, and the man is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses CUR to RUC; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a frill of fabric that is pleated or bunched together for trimming a dress.

clue.text: Being haughty, I leave idyll, or transform it

indicators.note: to transform is to change the form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the letter I leaves the word idyll, so it is removed from it

explanation.surface: A proud person choosing to quit a rural paradise or change it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I leave' takes I out of IDYLL, leaving DYLL; 'transform it' rearranges DYLL with OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordly behaviour is arrogant and imperious, as a nobleman might act towards inferiors.

clue.text: Disinfectant approved of at home

parts.note: formal means officially sanctioned or approved
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A cleaning product that has the official stamp of approval for household use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Formalin is a solution of formaldehyde in water used to sterilise and to preserve specimens.

clue.text: Abandoned hotel to die in transit, in America

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A grim story of a hotel deserted, left to decay while someone was travelling in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US a transit is a surveyor's instrument for measuring angles; the surface makes it sound like a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: American surveyors call their angle-measuring telescope a transit, the same instrument used in Britain for mapping land.

clue.text: Folk maybe browned off, as burns the outcome?

indicators.note: the outcome of the words is what they turn into when their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether people who are fed up get that way because sunburn is the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'browned off' means fed up in British slang, but here it is literal: tanned. The question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: People lying in the sun come away tanned, so they are an example of folk turned brown.

clue.text: Corrupt count ran off — left by night

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters of the word count are rearranged
off means awry or wrong, so the letters of the word ran are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked nobleman who fled, leaving under cover of darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' poses as a crooked nobleman fleeing, but 'Corrupt' rearranges it to NOCTU and 'off' rearranges RAN to RNA; 'by night' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal means occurring or active at night, like owls and bats.

clue.text: Stone in ring chum displayed

parts.note: O is a ring because of its shape
a pal is a chum

explanation.surface: A friend showing off a gem set in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'displayed' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent gemstone.

clue.text: Rash step to take? Another way may be the more knife-edged

indicators.note: putting the letters another way means rearranging them into a different order

explanation.surface: A warning that a hasty move could leave one even more precarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' and 'may be' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade with the keenest edge cuts best; the superlative of keen-edged.

clue.text: Insect here in a flash?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a bug turns up in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a small bloodsucking parasite, and in Britain a tick is also a moment, as in 'back in a tick'.

clue.text: Role reversal, agent turned hunter

indicators.note: a reversal turns the word for a role backwards

parts.note: a part is a role played by an actor

indicators.note: turned round, the word for agent reads backwards

parts.note: a rep, representative, is an agent

explanation.surface: A double-cross in which a spy switches sides to become a predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversal' turns PART into TRAP and 'turned' turns REP into PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapper is someone who catches wild animals, often for their fur.

clue.text: One god's to be worshipped — him, not some other!

indicators.note: made other, the letters of the three words are changed into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A declaration that only one deity should receive worship and no rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a creed: belief that a single god alone is to be worshipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotheism is the doctrine that there is only one deity.

clue.text: Doctor has various diets to suit couturier

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

indicators.note: various means differing, so the letters of the word diets are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor with a range of diets to fit a fashion designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges DIETS into DISTE; 'has' and 'to suit' are links, with 'suit' playing on clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A modiste is a fashionable dressmaker or milliner.

clue.text: Fellow Italian, carefree of carriage

indicators.note: set free, the letters of the word care are loosed into a new order

explanation.surface: A carefree Italian man and the way he carries himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'carefree' does double duty in the surface: its first half is the fodder and its second half, 'free', rearranges it to ACRE. 'carriage' means a vehicle, not deportment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiacre is a small four-wheeled horse-drawn hackney cab, once common in Paris.

clue.text: Worried about oil plant

indicators.note: worried means agitated or shaken, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: the fodder as the setter meant it, with N in place of one O

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about oil at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the fodder has an O where the answer needs an N, a slip in the clue; 'plant' looks like an industrial site but is a flowering shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Abutilon is a genus of shrubs in the mallow family, known as flowering maple.

clue.text: Told what to say when charged

explanation.surface: A witness coached on what to say once accused.
explanation.definitionFit: To prime someone is to brief them in advance, and a primed gun or charge is loaded and ready to fire.

clue.text: Builder thus divides the human race

indicators.note: the word for thus goes into and splits the word for humankind

parts.note: man means humankind
so means thus

explanation.surface: A grand claim that a builder splits humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the human race' is a long-winded way of saying mankind; 'divides' tells you the small word for 'thus' sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a worker in stone or brick.

clue.text: Tree is right under a church

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting one piece under another places it after

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A tree stands properly beneath a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the genus of maples, often grown as ornamental trees.

clue.text: Parking, I can activate alarm

parts.note: P is the symbol for parking

indicators.note: to activate is to set in motion, so the letters of the two words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver claiming they can set off a car alarm while parked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'activate' rearranges I CAN into ANIC; 'alarm' looks like the car device, but means fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden fear, a sense of alarm.

clue.text: Gets bigger when folded?

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that grows when it is creased.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN CREASES, the answer means folded.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase is to grow, and something in creases has been folded.

clue.text: E'er vile disaster strikes, bring succour

indicators.note: when disaster strikes things are thrown into chaos, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A poetic call to help whenever calamity hits.
explanation.walkthrough: E'er is a poetic contraction of ever.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve is to ease suffering or help someone in distress.

clue.text: A long train?

parts.note: read as a lengthy railway service, but really the group of attendants that trails behind a dignitary

explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a body of attendants following an important person, like a train of followers.
